routine_summary: Up at six, reviews the books in his study, at the cafe by a quarter to seven to oversee opening.
voice_card: Speaks in ledgers and verdicts; every sentence sounds like a final decision.

small_talk.greeting: What is it? I'm a busy man.
small_talk.how_are_you: I have a business to run and a murder on my premises. How do you think I am?
small_talk.occupation: I own Hobbs Cafe. I built it from the ground up.
small_talk.how_can_help: I've already told your officers everything I know.
small_talk.favorite_thing: I appreciate a quiet evening and a balanced ledger.
small_talk.about_me: I'm a businessman, Detective. Hard work and discipline. That's all there is to me.
small_talk.general_relationships: I employ half this village and extend credit to the rest. I don't need to be liked.
small_talk.emotions: Efficiency makes me happy. Incompetence, on the other hand, angers me.

routine_summary: Lives above the cafe. Down by half six to prep, opens the doors at eight sharp.
voice_card: Precise and clipped; clips her sentences even shorter when defensive, and never volunteers more than was asked.

baseline.habit_text: she rounds every answer up into a story, with one more character in it than you asked about
baseline.deviation_cue: The stories have stopped. Every answer now is exactly as long as it has to be, and not a word longer.

small_talk.how_are_you: I'm managing. We all have jobs to do, despite... everything.
small_talk.occupation: I manage Hobbs Cafe. I make sure everything runs like clockwork.
small_talk.how_can_help: I'll answer your questions if I can.
small_talk.favorite_thing: A perfectly organised stockroom. It's the little things.
small_talk.about_me: I keep my head down and do my work. I prefer not to get involved in village drama.
small_talk.general_relationships: I know everyone who comes in for coffee, but I keep my distance.
small_talk.emotions: A smooth morning rush is satisfying. Prying questions make me uncomfortable.

baseline.routine_summary: Morning delivery round through the square and rear alley; usually cadges a coffee when the cafe opens.
baseline.voice_card: Rambles cheerfully, over-explains when nervous, and tends to answer a question you didn't ask.

baseline.habit_text: his hands sketch every route and parcel in the air while he talks
baseline.deviation_cue: His hands have quit the conversation — flat on his knees while his mouth does all the work alone.

small_talk.how_are_you: Bit rattled to be honest! It's not every day this kind of thing happens.
small_talk.occupation: I'm a delivery driver. I do the morning rounds for most of the shops here.
small_talk.how_can_help: I see a lot on my route, so ask away! Happy to help.
small_talk.favorite_thing: Can't beat a good cup of coffee and a chat in the morning.
small_talk.about_me: Just a local guy making rounds. Try to keep a smile on my face, you know?
small_talk.general_relationships: I get along with just about everyone! Hard not to when you're delivering their parcels.
small_talk.emotions: A bit of sunshine and a friendly face make my day. Secrets and sneaking around... not my style.

baseline.routine_summary: Opens the bookshop at nine; mornings are for paperwork and coffee at Hobbs.
baseline.voice_card: Measured, almost rehearsed; pauses before answering and chooses polite words with visible care.

baseline.habit_text: she sits half out of the chair, as if the next task is already calling her name
baseline.deviation_cue: She has stopped moving. The woman with three tasks queued behind this one is sitting perfectly, unnaturally still.

small_talk.how_are_you: I am composed, thank you. Though the atmosphere is undeniably tense.
small_talk.occupation: I own the bookshop across the square. A quiet trade, usually.
small_talk.how_can_help: If I have observed anything of use, I will share it.
small_talk.favorite_thing: A rare first edition and an hour of silence.
small_talk.about_me: I came here for a quieter life. I tend my shop and mind my own business.
small_talk.general_relationships: I maintain cordial, professional relationships. Nothing more.
small_talk.emotions: I find satisfaction in order and literature. Chaos... unsettles me.

baseline.routine_summary: In the timber yard from early; takes deliveries around half seven.
baseline.voice_card: Blunt, short sentences, no hedging; gets louder rather than more careful when pressed.

baseline.habit_text: he leaves a workman's pause before each answer, measuring twice before he commits
baseline.deviation_cue: The pauses have doubled. He is testing every question for load before he puts any weight on it.

small_talk.how_are_you: I'm busy, that's how I am. Got a yard to run.
small_talk.occupation: I'm a builder. I run the timber yard and do most of the heavy lifting in this town.
small_talk.how_can_help: Look, if you have a question, just ask it so I can get back to work.
small_talk.favorite_thing: A job done right and getting paid on time.
small_talk.about_me: I work with my hands. I don't have time for gossip or games.
small_talk.general_relationships: People pay me to fix things, and some people owe me money. That's the extent of it.
small_talk.emotions: An honest day's pay makes me happy. People messing me about makes me furious.

baseline.routine_summary: Opens up the bookshop stockroom early, then shelves new deliveries.
baseline.voice_card: Soft-spoken and apologetic; qualifies everything ('I think', 'maybe') and trails off under pressure.

baseline.habit_text: she watches your face while she answers, checking that the words are landing right
baseline.deviation_cue: She has stopped checking your face. Her answers go to the table now, and stay there.

small_talk.how_are_you: I'm... okay, I think. It's just all a bit frightening.
small_talk.occupation: I assist Isabella at the bookshop. Unpacking, shelving... that sort of thing.
small_talk.how_can_help: I... I don't know if I can be much help, but I'll try.
small_talk.favorite_thing: I love the smell of the new paperbacks when we open the boxes.
small_talk.about_me: I'm nobody important, really. Just trying to keep out of everyone's way.
small_talk.general_relationships: Everyone is mostly nice to me. I try not to cause any trouble.
small_talk.emotions: A quiet afternoon with a good book makes me happy. Shouting... I really don't like shouting.

baseline.routine_summary: Early shift at the clinic; crosses the square a few times each morning.
baseline.voice_card: Calm, clinical phrasing; states observations like chart notes and avoids speculation.

baseline.habit_text: her voice carries the unhurried warmth of someone used to talking people back to calm
baseline.deviation_cue: The warmth has drained out of her voice. The words are the same; the bedside manner is gone.

small_talk.how_are_you: I am quite alright. In my line of work, you learn to compartmentalise.
small_talk.occupation: I'm a nurse at the clinic. I handle the early shift mostly.
small_talk.how_can_help: I'll provide whatever factual information I can.
small_talk.favorite_thing: A properly sterilised workspace. And a good cup of tea.
small_talk.about_me: I deal in facts and symptoms, Detective. I leave the stories to Elias.
small_talk.general_relationships: I see people when they are vulnerable. I keep their secrets, and they respect my privacy.
small_talk.emotions: Helping people recover gives me purpose. Senseless tragedy just makes me tired.

baseline.routine_summary: First on the square bench every morning with a flask and opinions.
baseline.voice_card: Talks like he's lecturing a classroom; fond of rhetorical questions and certain of every detail.

baseline.habit_text: he answers before the question has quite finished, a teacher who has heard every excuse in the room
baseline.deviation_cue: The interruptions have stopped. He waits out the whole question now, and answers only the part he has chosen.

small_talk.greeting: Ah, the authorities. Step into my office—well, my bench.
small_talk.how_are_you: Never better, Detective. The village hasn't seen this much excitement in decades!
small_talk.occupation: I'm a retired schoolteacher. Though some say I'm the village historian now.
small_talk.how_can_help: Ask me anything! I see everything from this bench, you know. Everyone's business.
small_talk.favorite_thing: A captive audience and a thermos of strong tea.
small_talk.about_me: I've lived here my whole life. Taught half the village how to read.
small_talk.general_relationships: I know everyone's past, their parents, and their secrets. They tolerate me, mostly.
small_talk.emotions: A good juicy scandal makes my morning. Being ignored... well, that's just rude.

baseline.routine_summary: Tends the fountain flowerbeds at first light, then sweeps the rear alley before the village wakes properly.
Does the morning post round through the square, the bookshop and the clinic before most doors have even opened.
Up before the ovens, delivers the morning loaves to the cafe and the bookshop, and always keeps the misshapen one back for herself.
Runs the milk round in strict order — cafe first, bookshop second — and rates every doorstep in the village by how promptly they bring the empties back.
Works his ladder clockwise around the square; swears the clinic's windows are the only ones anyone ever thanks him for.
Trundles his stall cart around the village testing pitches; has moved 'the perfect spot' four times this year and defends each one loudly.
Walks three dogs that aren't hers on a route their owners never chose; the terrier decides when they stop, and it always stops at the fountain.
Sets the papers out from the fountain to the cafe and reads every front page aloud to whoever stands still long enough.
Tunes the fiddle by the square until her fingers warm up, then follows the smell of coffee to the cafe pitch.
Sweeps the shopfronts in the order the village wakes — cafe, bookshop, clinic — and knows everyone's doormat better than they do.
